FAST

BERLIN, Nov 15 : FIFA president Gianni Infantino should be replaced as he has made world football's governing body worse than it was under disgraced former chief Sepp Blatter, Germany coach Juergen Klopp said on Sunday. Speaking a day before Germany's Nations League game against the Netherlands, Klopp said the situation at FIFA was potentially worse than under Blatter, who stepped down amid a corruption scandal and later faced criminal charges. "The opinion is unanimous that a change would make sense," Klopp told a press conference. "I didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone managed to do just that." Infantino, also Swiss, was elected FIFA president in 2016 after a corruption scandal brought Blatter's tenure to an end. Blatter was later acquitted in a Swiss criminal case concerning a two-million-Swiss-franc payment to former UEFA president Michel Platini.

"At the moment we think that if Infantino goes that then the next one could maybe do it better. I think it is possible to make it better," Klopp said. "There are certainly people out there who care about the future of football and have no financial interest linked to that, and if they come together and one of them would become president, it would be helpful." Infantino, who is up for re-election in March 2027 and who has vowed to stay on, came under heavy criticism in July after an unsuccessful attempt to bring private investors into a new FIFA commercial entity holding rights linked to competitions, including the World Cup.

FAST

LONDON, Nov 15 : London City Lionesses tightened their grip on third place in the Women's Super League after goalkeeper Mary Earps produced a string of superb saves, including a stunning late intervention, to secure a 1-1 draw at Arsenal on Sunday. Earps finished with eight saves in her third start for Lionesses, preserving a valuable point in the closing stages when Frida Maanum lofted an audacious effort towards the top corner, only for the former England goalkeeper to get the slightest touch on the ball and divert it onto the crossbar. The visitors had fought back from an early setback through Isobel Goodwin, whose equaliser came barely a minute after Maanum had given Arsenal the lead in the 10th minute with a composed finish from Alessia Russo's cutback. Arsenal, who have yet to win a league game at home this season, looked set to take control at the Emirates Stadium when Russo burst into the area and pulled the ball back for Maanum to sweep into the bottom corner.

But London City responded immediately as Goodwin broke free of Leah Williamson and rifled a powerful finish high into the net to silence the home crowd. "It's obviously a big point away from home," Earps told Sky Sports. "I thought either team probably could have won it in terms of chances, a lot of counter-attacking. "But really happy that we got the point. Would have liked three, so we'll go back to the training ground and work out how we could have made that difference to get the three points." Arsenal pressed for a winner after the break, but Earps repeatedly frustrated the hosts and capped her display with the dramatic late save from Maanum's looping effort. The eight saves were her most in a WSL game since 2017. The result kept London City third on 20 points, six behind leaders Chelsea, while Arsenal remained sixth on 14 points. "It all becomes one big blur, and you're sort of hoping the ref's going to blow the whistle," said Earps, who joined London City in the close season after two years at Paris St Germain. "But all the girls put their body on the line, and obviously I love defending the goal, I love making saves. So anything I can do to help the team and use that energy from a save to gain us some momentum." Earlier on Sunday, Mathilde Harviken struck in the 76th minute to earn Aston Villa a 1-0 win over Birmingham City, leaving Villa seventh and Birmingham 13th. Viviane Asseyi scored either side of halftime as West Ham United beat bottom side Charlton Athletic 2-0. West Ham climbed to ninth, while Charlton remained without a point after 10 league matches.

Source: Reuters

Nov 15 : Brazilian World Cup winner Ronaldinho played his first competitive match in 11 years at the age of 46, starting for Italian third-tier side Ravenna in their derby against Forli on Sunday. Wearing the number 10 shirt, Ronaldinho played the entire first half. At the interval, he took a lap of the pitch at the Stadio Bruno Benelli, waving to supporters as they stood to applaud him. Ravenna beat Forli 2-0 in the Serie C clash. Ronaldinho played a part in Giulio Donati's 36th-minute opener and Simone Rabbi added the second in the 58th. “It was lovely to be here, playing, having the build-up in the dressing room,” Ronaldinho told Sky Sport Italia. He said he had enjoyed playing alongside team mates who had grown up watching him.

Nov 15 : Russia will miss the 2027 World Junior Championship because of entry restrictions imposed by the Canadian government, the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) confirmed on Sunday. The IIHF said it had considered alternative arrangements but decided Canada would remain as host, with the tournament proceeding from December 26 to January 5 in Edmonton and Red Deer. Citing Russia's war in Ukraine, Canada's Secretary of State for Sport Adam van Koeverden told Reuters on Wednesday that Canada would deny entry to Russian and Belarusian athletes and officials coming to compete, even those with valid visas. The IIHF suspended teams from both countries in 2022 after Moscow launched its invasion from Russian and Belarusian territory, although last month’s Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling ordered the federation to readmit Russian teams to five championships.

The World Juniors were the first of the five tournaments covered by the October 30 ruling. The IIHF said it disagreed with the ruling but would comply. Prime Minister Mark Carney had previously said Canada would not permit Russian athletes to compete for their country on Canadian soil, a statement some perceived as keeping the door open for their participation as neutrals. Van Koeverden said Canada allowed neutral participation only by individual athletes, ruling out that option for the Russian team. The Russian Ice Hockey Federation called the IIHF's decision "unacceptable and unlawful" and said it would appeal to the International Olympic Committee to resolve the situation. "The IIHF's decision was made solely due to political reasons," it said in a statement. "The exclusion of the Russian national team violates fundamental legal principles, Olympism, the principle of non-discrimination, equality among athletes and the integrity of international tournaments." NORWAY BACK  The Norwegian Ice Hockey Association said its under-20 team had been reinstated after previously being told it would have to make way for Russia as the lowest-ranked side in the tournament. "We’re very happy for the players, the coaches and everyone in Norwegian ice hockey, who earned this place by winning promotion last year," association secretary general Petter Salsten said. “The team have been looking forward to this for a whole year but have spent the past month in limbo.” Norway said its pre-tournament training camp and games in Canada would go ahead as planned. Russia's potential return to international ice hockey has prompted boycott threats ahead of next year's men's World Championship in Germany. Austria, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, Latvia, Norway and Sweden have said they would refuse to face Russia. One sponsor has withdrawn, while others have said they could follow if Russia take part. The German Ice Hockey Federation urged the IIHF to provide clarity over the men's World Championship. "We now need this planning security for our home World Championship in May, for the teams, the fans and all partners," federation chairman Frank Lutz said in a statement. "We therefore demand prompt clarification from the IIHF." Russian President Vladimir Putin said earlier this month that countries opposing rulings allowing Russia to return to international sport were violating the rights of Russian athletes and democratic institutions.

Source: Reuters

LONDON, Nov 15 : England starters Seb Atkinson, Ollie Chessum and George Furbank have all been cleared to train again ahead of next Saturday's Nations Championship clash against New Zealand. The trio were injured in the 45–22 victory over Australia at the start of the month's programme and missed Saturday's 78-15 victory over Japan, England's record score in the fixture. Uncapped Harlequins flanker Jack Kenningham has also been called up to a 36-man squad in place of the injured Tom Curry, the Rugby Football Union said on Sunday. A win over New Zealand would give England a chance of finishing top of the Northern Hemisphere section and taking a place in the November 29 final of the inaugural competition.

(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Toby Davis)

INDIAN WELLS, California, Nov 15 : Women's Tennis Association Chair Valerie Camillo said she expects a return to "normal operations, normal financials" in 2027 and that she has full confidence in its outlook despite reports the tour could run short of cash. The Telegraph reported in September that the WTA projects operating losses of $23 million this year, adding that its accounts could move into the red by autumn 2027. Camillo did not directly address the reported figures when asked in an interview with Reuters at the WTA Finals, but said that 2026 was a year of transition. More than a billion people watched women's tennis last year, leaving it well placed for growth, she said.

"Everyone should be very confident in the future of the WTA," she said. RELOCATION COSTS This year, the tour absorbed the unexpected cost of moving the season-ending event to Indian Wells, after deciding to end an agreement under which Riyadh hosted the Finals with the backing of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF). The WTA ended the three-year deal after two years to secure certainty over where the event would be held, given uncertainty in the region, she said. Camillo said the tour took on the full financial investment of staging the tournament and was also funding the Finals prize money pool in full. She described the PIF as a continuing partner, noting that it still sponsors the tour's maternity fund and is a sponsor of this year's Finals. Pressure on finances is also tied to CVC Capital Partners, which acquired a 20 per cent stake in the WTA's commercial arm in 2023 for $150 million paid over five years. That funding, about $30 million a year, ends in 2027. EQUAL PRIZE MONEY Asked about criticism that the CVC money had gone too heavily into prize money, Camillo said equal pay was the foundation of the tour and that prize money would not be cut. She said all combined WTA-ATP Masters 1000 events would offer equal prize money next year, joining the Grand Slams. The WTA has not yet set prize money for the 2027 Finals. In September, Camillo said the tour was considering alternatives including a profit-sharing model with players. This year's total prize pool of $10 million is a drop from $15.5 million in 2025. Camillo also described a new Tournament Investment Fund, designed to help tournaments keep strong player fields and to support events in weaker calendar slots. It is part of the 2027 calendar overhaul after players asked for lighter commitments. Under the changes, the number of WTA 500 events each player is committed to will fall from six to four. CHARLOTTE AND TOUR UNIFICATION The WTA will stage the Finals in Charlotte, North Carolina, for at least three years from 2027. The event will be indoors at the Spectrum Center, home of the NBA's Charlotte Hornets. That could shrink the Finals from their current eight-day run down to five days to accommodate the NBA's schedule. Camillo said a format is being developed with players and an announcement is expected soon. She also said talks continue on closer cooperation between the men's and women's tours, but said any deal must be right for the women's game and protect its marketing profile. Camillo also cited new initiatives such as a collaboration with TikTok and one with Mercedes-Benz, which will see the winner of Sunday's final driving away with an SL 55 in the WTA's signature purple color. "We continue our really strong commercial growth, attracting new partnerships, and we're now self-operating our Finals, our media rights, our production," she said. "Our future trajectory is incredible."

Source: Reuters

EDINBURGH, Nov 15 : Scotland held on for a narrow 15-12 win over Australia in the Nations Championship at Murrayfield on Sunday, deepening the gloom for next year's World Cup hosts. Both sides scored two tries in an attritional and error-ridden battle that featured few moments of quality and a scoreless spell lasting more than 45 minutes. Matt Fagerson and Jack Dempsey went over for Scotland in the opening 27 minutes and Finn Russell added a conversion for a 12-5 halftime lead.  Russell's penalty stretched the advantage to 15-5 with six minutes remaining, before Max Jorgensen crossed in the final minute and Ben Donaldson converted. Australia had opened their account through winger Harry Potter's first-half try.

It was an eighth successive loss in Europe for the Wallabies, who showed early promise when new coach Les Kiss took over in August but now look devoid of confidence and in a rut. Australia had been heavily beaten by England at Twickenham a week earlier. Captain Harry Wilson said Sunday's performance represented a significant improvement, but the losing run leaves them under growing pressure with less than a year before their home World Cup kicks off on October 1. CAPTAIN MISSES OUT THROUGH INJURY Scotland overcame the overnight loss of captain Sione Tuipulotu to injury with his replacement Tom Jordan setting up the first try in the eighth minute. Scrumhalf Ben White's pass picked out Fagerson, who was alone on the touchline and went over to give Scotland the lead. Australia responded within three minutes after a sustained attack, flyhalf Carter Gordon delaying his pass before releasing Potter to score as Russell missed the tackle. Former Wallaby Dempsey finished off a pick and go, with Ewan Ashman and Fagerson driving towards the line and Dempsey carrying it over to put Scotland back ahead 12-5. There were no more points until the 74th minute when Australia were penalised for not clearing away at the ruck and Russell tucked over the penalty for a 10-point lead. But Australia then suddenly burst into life and threatened to set up a dramatic comeback as Jorgensen finished off some slick handling with less than a minute left on the clock. There was still time for Australia to collect the kick-off from Scotland and look for a winning try. They found some room on the left wing to threaten another score before being bundled into touch to end the contest. “It was a bit of an arm wrestle. Conditions played a part in that. It was a battle of the defences,” said Rory Darge, who captained the Scots in place of Tuipulotu. (Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Toby Davis)

WASHINGTON, Nov 15 : US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday said Nvidia needs to "go outside the company" as it seeks a new chief executive after Jensen Huang abruptly stepped down last week. Huang stepped down on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy, plunging the chipmaker into crisis. "This makes me think that as the board conducts a search for a new leader that they need to go outside the company, that just (with) what was going on inside the company, they need a dramatic shakeup," Bessent told Fox News' "Sunday Morning Futures" show. Bessent also said Nvidia's board and outside counsel needed to answer, within the next 10 days, questions about the company's culture of compliance with export restrictions. Nvidia's board has approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential replacement for Huang, the Financial Times said on Friday.

Source: Reuters

TURIN, Nov 15 : World number one Alexander Zverev eased past debutant Rafael Jodar in straight sets on Sunday to score an opening group win at the start of the ATP Finals in Turin. The German, a two-time champion at the season-ending tournament of the top eight players, bagged a break in each set to clinch a 6-4 6-4 victory over the 20-year-old Spaniard, who has played a sensational first season on tour and has risen from the mid-100s to the top 10 in less than 12 months. Jodar, however, could do little to tame Zverev's booming serve and the most experienced ATP Finals player in the field, playing his 31st match, earned a break to go 4-3 up with a superb backhand down the line. The Spaniard had two rare break chances at 5-4 behind but could not convert either. Instead Zverev bagged the set in the next game and grabbed a break early in the second set to open up a 3-1 lead.

Nov 15 : Rory McIlroy secured a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title on Sunday, matching Colin Montgomerie's mark for the most Order of Merit victories in European Tour history before dedicating the achievement to his recovering father. The 37-year-old Northern Irishman carded a bogey-free 67 to seal a fifth consecutive Race to Dubai crown, edging Spain's Eugenio Chacarra in the season-long standings. Englishman Tyrrell Hatton, meanwhile, cruised to a five-shot victory at the DP World Tour Championship. The latest crown capped another fine year for McIlroy, who successfully defended his Masters title at Augusta National in April to secure a second green jacket and further cement his place among the game's greats.

"I don't really know what to say. Winning eight Order of Merits was never really in my list of goals when I was growing up," McIlroy told Sky Sports. "I remember Monty (Montgomerie) being a stalwart of the European Tour. Going to watch him at the World Match Play at Wentworth over the years, I remember playing with him for the first time at the London Club on the European Tour in 2008. "To pull up alongside him and win eight of these things, it means the world to me. "I'm a proud European. I'm a proud European player and I'm proud to be a part of the DP World Tour and I'm very proud of myself right now." The milestone carried added emotional significance for McIlroy, whose father has spent the past two months recovering from major surgery. "He's been in the hospital for the last two months. He underwent a huge operation at the end of September, and he's recovering well, thankfully," McIlroy said. "But when I left to come here to the Middle East, I went up to Cleveland to see him before I went. He said to me: 'Go win the Race to Dubai.'"

BARCELONA, Nov 15 : Spanish second division team Tenerife returned to action on Sunday for the first time since the death of striker Jesus De Miguel, with emotional tributes before and during their game against Ceuta. De Miguel died on November 3, a day after colliding with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a league match at home. Tributes took place around the country and on Sunday at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium, Tenerife paid their own respects. A lengthy standing ovation bookended a minute of silence before the match. In the ninth minute play was stopped and a further round of applause followed, while a video of De Miguel was shown around the stadium, as occurred in all first and second tier games in Spain last weekend.

Tenerife fans also unfurled a banner reading "Jesus De Miguel, 9, eternally blue and white." Tenerife forward Nacho Gil opened the scoring in the 40th minute and he celebrated by holding up De Miguel's shirt to the crowd. Gil then revealed a message written under his shirt saying "Demi (De Miguel's nickname), always in our hearts." Neal Viereck added a second four minutes from time to seal a 2-0 win for Tenerife, ending a run of six games without a win. Tenerife are 14th in the Segunda standings, while Ceuta are bottom.  Last Saturday Tenerife's game with Granada was postponed and the club invited fans to the stadium to pay their respects to De Miguel. The squad and staff were present at the Heliodoro and in Navahermosa three days earlier, where De Miguel was laid to rest.
